_readme: Expected TEAM standings for G6, one entry per scoring-config variant.
HAND-COMPUTED. Never generated from lib/scoring/ — a fixture derived from the code under
test proves only that the code agrees with itself.
Every variant replays the SAME contest (fixtures/scoring/golden-team-contest.json) with a
different config, so flipping a config flag is a provable change rather than a hoped-for one.
The arithmetic for each is written out in its own _why block and in docs/SCORING.md §4.

_why: All defaults, and the organizer-confirmed reading. Group points go INSIDE the per-player
mean; side activity points are added FLAT.
groupPointsInsideMean: false. Group points are added to the team total AFTER the mean, so a
group problem is worth teamSize times as much — 125 to a team of four rather than 31.25.
A defensible format that makes the group round decisive. Not the one Coding Night runs.
sideActivitiesFlat: false. Side activity points go through the same divisor as everything
else, so a bigger team gets less credit for a puzzle it solved as a unit.
Cubs:     (400 + 100) / 2 + 0 / 2    = 250.00  (unchanged — Cubs have no side points)
THE ANSWER THE REAL SPREADSHEET PRODUCED, AND IT IS WRONG.
The sheet computed Panthers as 512.5:
That is the formula with the GROUP POINTS DROPPED ENTIRELY — the 125 never enters. The team
was under-credited by 31.25 points.
This is not a rounding disagreement or a difference of interpretation. It is a spreadsheet
formula that missed a cell, and eliminating exactly this class of error is why this platform
exists.
It is pinned here so a test can assert we do NOT reproduce it. Without that assertion, a
regression that silently dropped group points again would look like agreement with history
— the most convincing possible disguise for a scoring bug.
NO CONFIG PRODUCES THIS NUMBER. If any variant ever equals it, that variant is broken.
